Guideline: Use gsap.quickTo() for 120fps Magnetic Pull and 3D Tilt
Description: gsap.quickTo() reuses a single optimized tween instance instead of allocating a new tween on every pointermove event.
Do: Create xTo = gsap.quickTo(el, 'x', { duration: 0.2, ease: 'power3.out' }) once on mount
Don't: Call gsap.to(el, { x, y }) inside a high-frequency mousemove listener
Code Good:
const xTo = gsap.quickTo(btn, 'x', { duration: 0.2, ease: 'power3.out' });
btn.addEventListener('pointermove', e => xTo((e.offsetX - w/2) * 0.25));

Guideline: Use GSAP Timelines with Explicit Hitstop Gap for Hero Actions
Description: GSAP timelines make multi-stage Game Feel (Anticipation -> Hitstop -> Impact -> Follow-Through) declarative and easily reversible.
Do: Chain anticipation (0.06s) -> hitstop pause ('+=0.08') -> elastic burst
Don't: Nest 4 levels of setTimeout callbacks for multi-stage hero animations
Code Good: gsap.timeline().to(btn, { scale: 0.93, duration: 0.05 }).to(btn, { scale: 1.06, duration: 0.18, ease: 'back.out(2)' }, '+=0.085').to(btn, { scale: 1, duration: 0.15 });

Guideline: Use GSAP Flip Plugin for Cross-Container Card Morphs
Description: When moving a card between columns or expanding a card into a modal, Flip.getState() + Flip.from() handles all transform inversions.
Do: Capture state = Flip.getState(targets), mutate DOM, then call Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.28, ease: 'power3.out' })
Don't: Manually calculate getBoundingClientRect deltas without accounting for scroll and nested transforms
Code Good: const state = Flip.getState('.card'); moveCardInDOM(); Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.28, ease: 'power3.out', absolute: true });
